name: Calligraphy and brush-lettering classes
summary: How expats find calligraphy and modern brush-lettering classes in Singapore — Chinese brush, pointed-pen, and workshop formats, plus kit lists before the first session.
body:
Calligraphy scenes here span Chinese brush traditions, Japanese/Korean adjacent practices, and Western pointed-pen / modern brush lettering workshops. Studios and community centres run one-off workshops and term courses.

## Pick a lane
- Chinese brush (ink, rice paper, posture basics)
- Pointed pen / copperplate-style English scripts
- Modern brush pens for envelopes and signage
- Kids’ holiday lettering crafts (different from classical discipline)

Ask which tools are provided; nibs and sumi ink ruin white shirts.

## How to choose
Prefer teachers who demo grip and posture live, not only finished Instagram reels. Class size matters for feedback. For bilingual kids, clarify whether the class teaches characters or only stroke play. Workshop vouchers make good trials before multi-week fees.

## Practical tip
Sit with sleeves rolled and a cloth under your elbow. Photograph your teacher’s exemplar grid — memory fades by the next condo practice night.
